s3-000-d733a4490d7cd2b7.wav.text: Start with what a tensor is, because it is less than you might think.

s3-001-27fee5e54121ae25.wav.text: Everything from the previous episode transfers unchanged.

s3-002-aa4dde57a4e27970.wav.text: Shapes, broadcasting, reductions, einsum, all identical.

s3-003-cc7d350a7f4a7382.wav.text: A torch tensor adds exactly three things.

s3-004-ebfce5b72871ccb9.wav.text: A device that the storage lives on, cpu or cuda zero.

s3-005-c483ca1d828c48eb.wav.text: Optional gradient tracking, which means the tensor records the operations applied to it so they can be replayed in reverse.

s3-006-713eb9e0998043a6.wav.text: And in place operations, spelled with a trailing underscore, which are fast and which autograd will sometimes refuse to differentiate through.

s3-007-706c138fdcb2c91f.wav.text: Two spelling traps to note now and save an hour later.

s3-008-fd12d5eaf594e487.wav.text: Torch says dim and keep dim where NumPy says axis and keep dims.

s3-009-9bf153ac976430dd.wav.text: And torch defaults to float thirty two where NumPy defaults to float sixty four.

s4-000-3801a1b3b48518b6.wav.text: Here is the single most important fact about autograd, and it is on screen.

s4-001-97aa4e1bbd32fcbf.wav.text: A tensor created with requires grad equals true is a leaf of a computation graph.

s4-003-5c0c89d85bdb3269.wav.text: Calling backward on a scalar walks that graph in reverse, applying the chain rule, and puts the result into each leaf's grad attribute.

s4-005-1bffcc8559d502dd.wav.text: We call backward three times on the same leaf.

s4-012-48a9e3c092812776.wav.text: It is exactly what makes gradient accumulation across micro batches work, which is how you train a model that does not fit in memory.

s4-013-b8cb0d6c82853954.wav.text: But it means every single training loop must clear the gradients before it starts.

s4-014-1b661b00d952df72.wav.text: And omitting that is the most common PyTorch bug there is, because the loss still goes down.

s4-015-8d69475a54db3fd4.wav.text: It just goes down using the sum of every gradient computed so far, and absolutely nothing tells you.

s5-000-11a9816b13520fd7.wav.text: Three more facts and you have the complete user's model of autograd.

s5-001-d8ff57fbbf364fcb.wav.text: First, calling backward on something that is not a scalar raises an error.

s5-002-43fe7863f512b255.wav.text: A loss is a scalar precisely so that the upstream gradient is implicitly the number one.

s5-003-8a88cc23967706f4.wav.text: For a vector you have to supply that gradient yourself.

s5-004-ad9d331f72193d1b.wav.text: Second, the graph is freed after backward runs.

s5-005-6126376de113a387.wav.text: Every forward pass builds a fresh one, and reaching for retain graph equals true is nearly always a sign that you meant to restructure something.

s5-006-ea6cdce29340aa62.wav.text: Third, intermediate tensors get no gradient attribute at all, because storing one per node would explode memory.

s5-007-38ef0a14d390bffb.wav.text: Retain grad opts a specific one in, which is useful for debugging and for the interpretability work in topic twenty two.

s5-008-633cafe3f4c4ed0e.wav.text: And finally, no grad stops the recording entirely, while detach cuts a single tensor out of the graph.

s5-009-affd8d46a56c7fb7.wav.text: Use no grad for evaluation and detach when you are storing a value for logging.

s5-010-4edbf97e47e103e5.wav.text: Confusing the two costs memory, not correctness.

s6-000-afe4b34e02a21425.wav.text: The model returns raw logits and never probabilities, and there is a reason worth stating three ways.

s6-002-22c486703c730487.wav.text: The sigmoid's derivative cancels against the logarithm in the cross entropy, leaving a gradient that is simply the prediction minus the target.

s6-004-dc07c1c90a2310b2.wav.text: The derivative of the loss with respect to the pre activation z is sigma of z, minus y, divided by n.

s6-007-870d77421dbd49d2.wav.text: And in code, you get that cancellation by using the fused loss, binary cross entropy with logits.

s6-008-c866e9ec4ca92196.wav.text: Applying a sigmoid yourself and then using plain binary cross entropy is mathematically identical and numerically worse.

s6-009-21c08ec9ae7e1a87.wav.text: The fused version uses the log sum exp trick internally.

s6-010-8e69676e2de7ae01.wav.text: The split version overflows once a logit reaches about plus or minus forty, and hands you a not a number.

s6-011-f16ef9391f605b2e.wav.text: The step three script writes this derivative out by hand in NumPy and matches PyTorch's autograd to two point eight times ten to the minus seventeen.

s6-012-cc890b3dbf763664.wav.text: Doing that once is what stops autograd from feeling like magic.
